reviews.title: Review
reviews.text: Babbel

reviews.title: Limited Lessons
reviews.text: Overall, the app has a useful and simple layout. Unfortunately, there are limited lessons and the use of adaptive learning is nonexistent.  It is disappointing. I would never spend the money to purchase this app when there are other others that are more adaptable.  I was so excited to start to use it until I reach the end and there were no more lessons.

reviews.title: Der Ton mancher Sprecher ist sehr schlecht.
reviews.text: Oft ist nicht zu verstehen was der Sprecher sagt. Er hat eine unangenehme, schrille Stimme. Vielleicht ist das gewollt, aber es ist definitiv schlecht umgesetzt.

reviews.title: You are not their focus
reviews.text: Babbel seems more focused on getting users through new lessons than helping them learn and retain what they’ve studied. Completing a lesson is only part of the process; meaningful progress also means remembering and being able to use the material later. The app offers few opportunities to revisit earlier lessons or practice past material, so you’re left to create your own review sessions. The practice activities that are available are often only one or two questions long and don’t provide enough reinforcement. I’d like to see more substantial, ongoing review built into the app.

reviews.title: Great Method, VERY limited languages
reviews.text: Was hoping for more options for languages to learn. Specifically, would love to see Mandarin, Japanese, and Arabic. But this is very Euro-centric and therefore not as comprehensive as I hoped.

reviews.title: Lernfortschritt
reviews.text: Das Lernprogramm ist unglücklich aufgebaut häufig werden gerade gelernte Themen dann abgefragt und dort taucht es aber in einer anderen Art und Weise wieder auf, so dass man zum Beispiel beim Adjektiv bilden immer auf die falsche Fährte geführt wird. Auch fehlt total ein Grammatik Grundkurs, dass man einmal weiß wie man Verben durch dekliniert und nicht immer nur anhand von Vorsätzen arbeitet. Also mir fällt das lernen mit Babbel leider sehr schwer.. ich würde die App daher nicht weiterempfehlen,

reviews.title: Beware pedatory subscription
reviews.text: App is fine but the subscription specifically does not go through the Apple App Store and is thus easily forgotten about until they charge you another $80 6 months later. Good luck.

reviews.title: Abzocke
reviews.text: Achtung, die hauen dir für 150.-ein Abo rein, wenn du das Testabo nicht rechtzeitig kündest. Übelste Geschäftspraxis. Im Kundendienst wirst du dann von der kI abgewimmelt. FINGER WEG, DA GIBT ES BESSERE ALTERNATIVEN.

reviews.title: Awful dated app
reviews.text:
I made the mistake of accidentally renewing my membership to this absolutely outdated and very poor app. The conversation function is very poor, this app is designed for those with a higher education or university qualification in language, such as English– you’ve got no hope if you’re just a Joe public trying to learn a foreign language – don’t bother, there’s better apps available. 
Even the much maligned Duolingo has a far better inclusive approach to language learning than this outdated, ridiculous old school app.

reviews.title: Boost false confidence
reviews.text: I completed B1 level in German and found out that the app did not actually cover many grammatical rules that one should know by the end of B1. It was absolutely wast of time but if you still find it hard to start you can take advantage of the gamification but if you want to learn try other alternatives.

reviews.title: Customer Service
reviews.text: I had worked with the app for about 5 months.  I tried to devote about 5 hours per week and I started noticing that I was answering questions by deduction rather than answering because I understood the question.  This became frustrating and I stopped using the app about 5 weeks ago.  Unfortunately, I forgot about the app until I received the automatic renewal notification on my most recent credit card statement.  I did not receive an email from Babbel notifying me that they would be billing me in the coming days, so I could cancel, like every other auto renewal subscription that I have does.  (Incidentally, I also checked my spam folder and there was no notification there either. However, there were multiple emails asking me to upgrade to the unlimited plan.) Anyway, I asked for a refund because it had only been 4 days since I was billed but Babbel refused because of their “terms”.  If you don’t wish to be viewed as a scam I suggest you at least send an email to your recurring subscription customers, so they customer can decide if they want to continue instead of you deciding for the customer after you capture their payment.

reviews.title: Male or female?
reviews.text:
In the very first dialogue in the very first lesson a lady meets a man that she hasn't seen for a while. They both say hi and he tells her she has a beautiful costume. She says thank you in the masculine but then apologize and says thank you in the feminine.
There is no explanation given but it is appears that man is identifying as a woman? Why add something so confusing to this language study?
This devalues the purpose of the lesson.

reviews.title: Horrible onboarding for intermediate learners, awful free experience
reviews.text:
I refuse to sign up for a free trial that my ADHD brain will forget about and be billed for, so I’m stuck with…. One… lesson… of flash cards as a free user. That’s it. That’s all. 

It asked my language level (beginner, intermediate, and advanced, with no explanation as to what each meant) and dumped me into something way lower than where I should be - without any test or assessment. How am I supposed to evaluate an app for effectiveness when they use predatory “free trial” tactics to lock any meaningful content behind a pay wall? I will happily give you money - if your app works for me. Do better by your free users. I would not recommend this app.

reviews.title: Problem with method
reviews.text: The lessons make it seem as though I’m learning. But, I don’t retain much of the information. I can get all of the questions correct in all of the lessons to a point. But I don’t feel as though I’m learning much of anything from this app. The majority of what I know comes from my past learning of the language. I’m a firm believer in hearing and learning to understanding ,then speaking what is heard before learning to read and write in a language. The lessons seem to mostly focus on reading and listening. Perhaps some learners prefer this method but it’s not the best method for me. I now wish that I could get a refund for the rest of my subscription.

reviews.title: Nonsensical Structure to Learning Does Not Build Confidence for the Student.
reviews.text: The app throws vocab, dialog and grammar at you with little to no explanation or foundation. There’s got to be concepts I need to learn. Not just a category of sentences the app chooses to focus on (restaurants, jobs, numbers). There’s no sense of building knowledge and confidence. Things are introduced with no explanation or reasoning. Want a place where you can hear or practice speaking or writing verb conjugations? Nope. How about a reference section on numbers in French I can always go back to? Days of the week, colors, directions, BASICS! Maybe you’ll see an example in a lesson, maybe not. I need LOTS of examples, repetition and different voices to learn pronunciation. There are no lessons on pronunciation (French). If I want to spend an hour practicing different variations of être, LET ME! The speaking feature is far too lenient. You can absolutely maul a french sentence and the app will accept it, when you *know* how bad your pronunciation is. I’ve finished the first series of lessons, about 10 days of study.

reviews.title: Poor Audio Quality
reviews.text:
The audio is poor. Every playback is clipped at the start. A simple example would be the word ‘Bonjour’, it is clipped to ‘njour’ similarly a word like ‘C’est’ is clipped to ‘st’. It is extremely frustrating and irritating. It is especially so when answering questions on sentences when the start of the sentence is missing. I’ve tried to reload the app, deleted ad blockers and anything else that may interfere with the audio. I’ve swapped to a different WiFi provider and tried using Babbel on a PC. All to no avail. 

Very poor quality for a not insignificant cost!!!!!

reviews.title: Do NOT buy this App if you are wanting to learn European Portuguese (Portugal)
reviews.text:
I will repeat what I wrote in the Review Title - Do NOT buy this App if you are wanting to learn European Portuguese (Portugal).  Their Portuguese course focuses on Brazilian Portuguese and not European Portuguese.  That is very disappointing to me as that is NOT what I wanted and they of course did not tell me that when they took my money.  When I used their AI help option to find out more about this, it says that they do not offer European Portuguese at this time.  They should tell people that up front before they take their money that you are not buying or getting what you think you are paying for.  They go on to say that “both versions are mutually understandable” but there are certainly differences in vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation between the two.  They go on to say that “you will still be able to communicate effectively with people from Portugal”.  Sorry but being able to likely get your point across to someone is absolutely not the same as learning the language of the country.   Tell people up front before they buy what version of Portuguese they will be learning.  

From reading reviews of the various apps available to learn to speak a language, Babbel seemed like a good option,  too bad they wanted my money more than they wanted to be honest and up front with me about what I was actually buying.  I guess I will be looking at other language learning apps now even though I bought a lifetime license from Babbel thinking that was the best way to go…

reviews.title: German version very out of date
reviews.text: This app continuously wants me to learn out dated and useless words.  Who in Germany calls a camera Fotoapparat? Who sends postcards and wants to buy stamps? If I complain I get a bot spouting platitudes.  I really want to improve my German but this app is way behind my current level and I can’t find a way to get to more useful lessons.  I cannot recommend.

reviews.title: ⚠️ Doesn’t Work with Basic iPhone Security Settings
reviews.text:
⚠️ This app is extremely frustrating to use.

❌ Basic functionality is unreliable. With iOS Lockdown Mode enabled, the app simply doesn’t work as expected — lessons fail to open, making it impossible to study. For a paid lifetime product, this is unacceptable. An app should not break under standard device security settings.

🔒 On top of that, the learning experience feels unnecessarily limited. The platform doesn’t provide enough flexibility in how users engage with language variations, which makes it feel restrictive rather than adaptive to real-world needs.

📉 Overall, this feels like a product with potential that is held back by poor technical compatibility and a lack of user-focused design. I expected far more, especially after paying for lifetime access.

reviews.title: Babbel is not a good language learning software:(
reviews.text:
Let me start this review off by stating that I have been learning another language for right over a month on this app and another. I also purchased the lifetime membership thinking it was a good deal.
With that said, Babbel is terrible at what they’re trying to do. The majority of what they’re teaching is written, which is an almost useless skill. It If I wanted to speak to someone in another language I could use Google Translate. The purpose is to speak another language where it is much harder to communicate face to face. I am still learning intros to conversations and I am expected to be able to spell 13-14 letter words in an alphabet I am just now learning. It hasn’t even taught me the entire alphabet but I am expected to remember the exact spelling or they simply say “wrong” and move along🙄 I can speak the majority of what it asks me, but I can not correctly spell it. Babbel can not differentiate and makes no attempt to see what you remember vocally. I recommend Duolingo for free if you want to start learning a language. Maybe this would be better if you were already adept.

reviews.title: Problems problems problems, NO ANSWERS FROM BABBEL
reviews.text: What started out as a promising language course has quickly evolved into something I wish I had never bothered with. The lesson content does not, on many sections, match the supposed lesson. Also, it has a quick review section, but then review material often bears no relation to the lessons covered, with words and lessons never covered being ‘Reviewed’. I have tried to let Babbels team know about this through the Support Chat area, but have not received any replies or noticed any change to the problems reported. They seem to follow Duolingo’s support system, whereby they ignore problems but always reply to positive comments. Wish I had never started this and could get my money back, FAT CHANCE!
